newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-THIRD ROUND PLAY IN MEMORIAL TOURNAMENT RESUMES.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-THIRD ROUND PLAY IN MEMORIAL TOURNAMENT RESUMES.

text.p: The third round of the rain-delayed Memorial Tournament resumed on Sunday and officials said the fourth round would be played on Monday.
Rain suspended play in the third round on Saturday after the leaders had played three holes. Play resumed at 2:30 p.m. EDT (1830 GMT) on Sunday.
At the halfway stage of the tournament Scott Hoch led the field with his 10 under par total, one stroke ahead of Tommy Tolles and Vijay Singh of Fiji.
The PGA Tour, as part of a new policy to complete tournaments, has decided to play the full 72 holes and have the players return for the fourth round on Monday.

U.S. Open qualifying rounds at several sites had been scheduled for Monday, with 18 players in the Memorial field scheduled to play in the 36 hole qualifying. But the USGA has pushed back the Columbus, Ohio area qualifying to Tuesday.

Two players in the Memorial field withdrew on Sunday -- Japan's Shigeki Maruyama, who had a neck injury, and Rick Fehr, who decided to fly back to Seattle for U.S. Open qualifying, though he had the option to do so at any other site on Tuesday.
